page.title: Memory, capacity and performance
page.description: What a tinyactors actor costs in memory, how to size a host, how each operation's cost holds as the population doubles, and its conformance to SCXML.

hero.headline: Small enough to use everywhere.
hero.lede: A started actor takes about 530 bytes and a hibernated one about 120. Four million fit in one process, and each operation costs about the same at four million actors as at two.

section.heading: An actor takes about 530 bytes.
section.p: Each cell is the resident memory one more actor, message or delayed send adds, with a million already in the process.

table.caption: Measured 2026-11-20 on an Intel Xeon at 2.10 GHz, 4 CPUs, 16 GiB, Linux; Node.js 22.23.5 and Bun 1.4.1. A counter chart with one variable, messages of {"text": "hello"}, tracing on.

section.p: A host's fixed costs spread over its actors, so an actor costs less in a larger population.

section.heading: Size a host.
section.p: A host grows on its own, but each growth copies its memory. A host that will hold a known population is better sized for it.
hostStats reports each pool's capacity, what it uses and its high water mark:

section.heading: Twice the actors, the same cost.
section.p: Each row times one operation of the API on two million actors and on four million. Each cell gives both costs and their ratio, and a test fails when a ratio passes 1.5.

table.section: Work does not grow with the population
table.caption: Most actors hibernated in SQLite, at most 1000 resident. Measured 2026-11-20 on an Intel Xeon at 2.10 GHz, 4 CPUs, 16 GiB, Linux; Node.js 22.23.5 and Bun 1.4.1. Microseconds.

section.heading: Measure it on your device.
section.p: Pick a scenario and a population, and one host fills and works in a Worker on this page.

playground.description: A host on this device fills with up to four million actors, then sends them events, lets them message each other, keeps most of them asleep in a store, or gives each a timer. Charts show its actors, memory, messages a second and time per message.

section.p: The charts show how many actors this device holds and how many messages a second it handles.
Every counter in the lab runs this chart: it waits for add and counts.

section.heading: Correct by the standard.
section.p: The core passes the W3C's SCXML test suite, and every binding runs it too.

claim.p: That is 158 mandatory tests and 33 optional ones, BasicHTTP included.

claim.statement: Every binding runs the same suite.
claim.p: The conformance suite runs the W3C tests and its own scenarios against each binding, on each of its datamodels.
